sections.heading: Opening
paragraphs: Per the file, fast, reliable synchronization is (per the file) the biggest reason Solana (per the file) is able to achieve such high throughput. Per the file, traditional blockchains synchronize on large chunks of txs called blocks. Per the file, by synchronizing on blocks, a tx cannot be processed until (per the file) a duration, called "block time", has passed. Per the file, in Proof of Work (per the file) consensus, these block times (per the file) need to be very (per the file) large \(~10 minutes\) to (per the file) minimize the odds of multiple nodes producing a new valid (per the file) block at the same time.

Per the file, there's no such constraint (per the file) in Proof of Stake consensus, (per the file) but without reliable timestamps, a node cannot determine the order of incoming blocks. Per the file, the popular workaround is (per the file) to tag each block (per the file) with a wallclock timestamp. Per the file, because of clock drift (per the file) and variance in network (per the file) latencies, the timestamp is (per the file) only accurate within an hour or two. Per the file, to workaround the workaround, (per the file) these systems lengthen block (per the file) times to provide reasonable (per the file) certainty that the median (per the file) timestamp on each block is always increasing.

Per the file, solana takes a very (per the file) different approach, which it (per the file) calls _Proof of History_ or _PoH_. Per the file, leader nodes "timestamp" blocks (per the file) with cryptographic proofs that (per the file) some duration of time (per the file) has passed since the last proof. Per the file, all data hashed into (per the file) the proof most certainly (per the file) have occurred before the proof was generated. Per the file, the node then shares (per the file) the new block with node nodes, which are able (per the file) to verify those proofs.

Per the file, the blocks can arrive at nodes in any order or (per the file) even could be replayed years later. Per the file, with such reliable synchronization (per the file) guarantees, Solana is able (per the file) to break blocks into smaller batches of txs called _entries_. Per the file, entries are streamed to nodes in realtime, before any (per the file) notion of block consensus. Per the file, solana technically never sends (per the file) a _block_, but uses (per the file) the term to describe (per the file) the sequence of entries that nodes vote on to achieve _confirmation_.

Per the file, in that way, Solana's confirmation times may be compared apples to apples (per the file) to block-based systems. Per the file, the current implementation sets (per the file) block time to 800ms. Per the file, what's happening under the (per the file) hood is that entries are streamed to nodes as quickly as a leader (per the file) node can batch a set of valid txs into an entry. Per the file, validators process those entries (per the file) long before it is (per the file) time to vote on their validity.

Per the file, by processing the txs optimistically, there is effectively (per the file) no delay between the (per the file) time the last entry (per the file) is received and the (per the file) time when the node can vote. Per the file, in the event consensus (per the file) is **not** achieved, a (per the file) node simply rolls back its state. Per the file, this optimistic processing technique (per the file) was introduced in 1981 (per the file) and called Optimistic Concurrency Control.

Per the file, it may be applied to blockchain (per the file) architecture where a cluster (per the file) votes on a hash (per the file) that represents the full (per the file) ledger up to some _block height_. Per the file, in Solana, it is (per the file) implemented trivially using the (per the file) last entry's PoH hash. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: Relationship to VDFs
paragraphs: Per the file, the Proof of History (per the file) technique was first described (per the file) for use in blockchain (per the file) by Solana in November of 2017. Per the file, in June of the (per the file) following year, a similar (per the file) technique was described at (per the file) Stanford and called a verifiable delay function or _VDF_. Per the file, a desirable property of (per the file) a VDF is that (per the file) verification time is very fast.

Per the file, solana's approach to verifying (per the file) its delay function is proportional (per the file) to the time it took (per the file) to create it. Per the file, split over a 4000 (per the file) core GPU, it is (per the file) sufficiently fast for Solana's (per the file) needs, but if you asked (per the file) the authors of the paper (per the file) cited above, they might tell (per the file) you \(and have\) that Solana's approach is algorithmically (per the file) slow and it shouldn't be called (per the file) a VDF.

Per the file, we argue the term (per the file) VDF should represent the (per the file) category of verifiable delay (per the file) functions and not just (per the file) the subset with certain performance characteristics. Per the file, until that's resolved, Solana (per the file) will likely continue using the (per the file) term PoH for its application-specific VDF. Per the file, another difference between PoH (per the file) and VDFs is that (per the file) a VDF is used (per the file) only for tracking duration.

Per the file, poH's hash chain, on (per the file) the other hand, includes hashes (per the file) of any data the application observed. Per the file, that data is a double-edged sword. Per the file, on one side, the (per the file) data "proves history" - that (per the file) the data most certainly (per the file) existed before hashes after it. Per the file, on the other side, (per the file) it means the application (per the file) can manipulate the hash (per the file) chain by changing _when_ (per the file) the data is hashed.

Per the file, the PoH chain therefore fails to serve as a good (per the file) source of randomness whereas (per the file) a VDF without that data could. Per the file, solana's leader rotation algorithm, as an illustration, is derived only from the (per the file) VDF _height_ and not its (per the file) hash at that height.

sections.heading: Relationship to Consensus Mechanisms
paragraphs: Per the file, proof of History is (per the file) not a consensus mechanism, (per the file) but it is used (per the file) to improve the performance (per the file) of Solana's Proof of Stake consensus. Per the file, it is also used (per the file) to improve the performance (per the file) of the data plane protocols.
